text.p: Spanish government bonds closed slightly higher on Wednesday drawing strength from labour reform proposals and expectations for moderating Spanish inflation.
Traders said there had been strong buying in two and three-year bonds and the short-end would continue to outperform in coming sessions.

"The long-end is looking a bit toppish and we saw some switching out of the long-end into the short this afternoon," said one trader. "There is still value in the short-end and so it will probably continue to outperform."
Traders said March CPI data due on Friday would continue to hold the market's attention for the timebeing. Analysts expect CPI to rise 2.4 percent year-on-year versus 2.5 pct in February.
Unions and employers' labour reform proposals lent some support to bonds, although traders were not overly impressed.
"They were marginally positive for the market but at the end of the day these reforms will do little to reduce unemployment," said one dealer.
